visual.general_description: Printed 12-lead electrocardiogram with a lead II rhythm strip.
visual.detailed_description: Black-on-white electrocardiogram printed on fine grid paper. The sheet shows a labeled 12-lead layout twice, once in the left half and once in the right half, separated by a thin vertical line: row one is labeled I, aVR, V1, V4; row two II, aVL, V2, V5; row three III, aVF, V3, V6 in each half. Each lead segment begins with a small rectangular calibration pulse at the left edge. A long rhythm strip labeled II runs across the bottom with "25mm/s" printed at its lower right. A solid black rectangle covers the top-left corner of the sheet above the first lead label. QRS complexes differ in shape between leads; V1 and V2 show the tallest deflections. No patient name, date or numeric heart-rate readout is visible.

visual.general_description: Anesthetic record chart with gas rows, SpO2 row, blood pressure and heart-rate grid and event labels.
visual.detailed_description: Anesthetic record on a bordered grid. A time header prints 10:00 at the top left, 10:30 near the center right and 10:45 at the top right. Three gas rows are labeled O2 (L/min), N2O (L/min) and Sevoflurane (%); each prints "5" at its left edge. A thin horizontal bar with an end tick extends along the O2 row to the right of the 10:30 mark, while the N2O and Sevoflurane bars are short and end near the left of the grid. An SpO2 row prints 100 in each of its nine column cells. Below is a vital-sign grid with a left legend: a downward V for systolic blood pressure, an upward V for diastolic blood pressure, a filled dot for heart rate, and a crossed mark for start and completion of anesthesia; the vertical axis prints 50, 100 and 150. Plotted V marks, up marks and dots are scattered across the columns; the heart-rate dots sit lowest at the second plotted point and are higher at the later points. A bottom event row has crossed marks at its left and right ends, with leader lines to printed labels: Physical restraint, Monitor set, Cardiac arrest, start cardiopulmonary resuscitation, Recovery of spontaneous circulation, Intravenous catheter insertion, Body movement and Recovery of consciousness.

visual.general_description: Three stacked lead II ECG strips showing regular complexes, then sparse complexes, then a flat trace.
visual.detailed_description: Three black-on-white monitor strips are stacked and labeled a, b and c at their upper left. Each carries a calibration pulse at the left, a lead II label with x1, an ART label with printed 200 and 0 scale marks, and a small black bar at the bottom center. Strip a has regularly spaced QRS complexes with T waves; strip b has a mostly flat baseline with two isolated complexes; strip c is a flat horizontal trace with no complexes visible.

panels.general_description: Lead II ECG strip with a printed monitor text block above regularly spaced broad QRS complexes.
panels.detailed_description: Black-on-white monitor strip on grid paper. A three-line text block at the top reads HR:85 PR:85 VPC:0 on the first line, ST(II):0.23 ST(V5): then dashes and mV on the second, and NIBP:113/47(78)mmHg followed by a clock time beginning 10:3 on the third. Lead labels II, V5 and EXT4, each with x1, sit down the middle. Several regularly spaced QRS complexes, each followed by a broad T wave, run across the strip. The HR digit and final time digit are low resolution.
